To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the noise delayed switching of long Josephson junctions is observed for the overdamped case, and that this effect is suppressed for junctions longer than several Josephson lengths.

(1) the noise delayed switching effect vanishes for junctions longer than several Josephson lengths, (2) the noise delayed decay effect is observed for junction lengths smaller than several Josephson length.
the noise induced delay of the switching of long Josephson junctions vanishes in the range of low noise intensities, for junctions longer than several Josephson lengths.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the influence of the junction length on the noise delayed switching of long Josephson junctions.
the influence of noise on the switching dynamics of long Josephson junctions.
the effect of noise on the switching process of long Josephson junctions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the noise delayed decay effect is observed only for the junctions with lengths of the order of several Josephson penetration depths and it disappears when the junction length is greater than several Josephsons penetration depths.
the effect of noise delayed switching is not observed for the long Josephson junctions.
the noise delayed decay effect is a property of the long junction dynamics, which vanishes for long junctions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the noise delayed decay is an effect of a transient dynamics and it does not exist for long enough junctions.
the noise delayed switching is a non-trivial phenomenon which is not observed for long junctions, while for shorter ones the noise delayed switching can be observed.
the noise delayed decay is an intrinsic effect of long Josephson junctions and is independent of the nature of the noise source.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the noise-induced delayed decay effect is a purely local phenomenon and it cannot be observed for the case when the noise correlation time is smaller than the Josephson penetration depth.
the noise induced delay in switching is a finite size effect.
the effect of noise delayed switching is not a universal property of the sine-Gordan model, and it is not a generic property of the Josephson junctions.
